maria: quick findings from today's profiler run on 8xA100 w/ TP=2 PP=2
aj: nice, what stood out?
maria: all-reduce time jumps when we pull KV shards across pipeline boundaries. spike at step ~3 of generation when KV cache fill happens. overall throughput drops ~18% vs replicated-KV baseline.
perf-bot: uploaded profile: https://internal.redwood/profiles/1783456789/kv-shard-run.html :bar_chart:
olga: can you paste the critical flame view? is it NCCL wait or host->dev memcpy?
maria: flame shows NCCL:allreduce and ncclGroupEnd dominating during ks=1..4 microbatches. small kernels (fwd attn) suffer because comm doesn't overlap. root cause seems to be uneven microbatch packing + KV pull barrier.
sachin: hmm. TP requires sharded params, PP introduces stage boundaries for KV. If KV is sharded across TP dim then PP stage needs remote access -> more all-reduce/point-to-point.
aj: agree. two levers: 1) change KV sharding to be local to PP stage (replicate across PP, shard across TP) 2) improve comm/compute overlap by batching NCCL ops + fuse small kernels.
maria: implemented a quick prototype: replicate KV per PP stage (i.e., shard only across TP & DP). re-ran: all-reduce overhead reduced, latency lower, but memory up ~12% -> still within Dedicated targets, but problematic for 4x A100 configs.
olga: tradeoff noted. any kernel-level wins?
maria: yes — switching to fused rotary+matmul kernel (kernel-v6) reduced per-token matmul time by 9% but increased register pressure -> less headroom for KV replication. Also noticed kernel change interacts with batching heuristics: smaller microbatches mean more frequent KV pulls.
sachin: for DP, replicated KV is natural (each replica holds full KV). But for large models that's impossible. Suggest dynamic policy: replicate KV for PP stages with short seqs or when batch-parallelism low; otherwise use TP-sharded KV with async prefetch.
aj: sounds good. also consider these batching heuristics:
- dynamic microbatch sizing based on seq-length histogram
- group small requests to form a prefix-batched kernel path
- prefetch KV for expected next tokens for left-to-right workloads
maria: prototype config used:
```
kv_shard_strategy: "tp_shard_pp_replicate_fallback"
prefetch: true
microbatch_target_tokens: 4096
nccl_grouping: true
```
olga: what's `nccl_grouping` do?
aj: groups small NCCL ops into a single all-reduce call when possible, then schedules kernel launches while the group is in-flight. helps overlap.
maria: perf numbers from today (8xA100, 2TPx2PPx2DP):
- baseline (replicated-KV, old kernels): 185 tokens/s
- TP-sharded KV across PP boundaries (current default): 152 tokens/s
- replicate per-PP-stage (maria prototype): 171 tokens/s
- replicate + kernel-v6 + nccl_grouping: 196 tokens/s (but mem +10%)
perf-bot: regression alert: recent PR #3785 (kernel-v5->v6) flagged increased peak SM usage on 2xA100 tests. See: https://ci.redwood/runtime/3785 :warning:
aj: interesting that kernel-v6 both helps and hurts. maybe we should gate it behind a mem check and an adaptive kernel selector.
olga: suggestion: runtime should expose a policy graph evaluator that picks (kv_shard_strategy, kernel_variant, batching_policy) per model+shape profile. then we can A/B test.
sachin: agree. add these telemetry hooks: per-request KV transfer bytes, NCCL op latency histogram, per-kernel SM occupancy. we need signal to detect when replicate-KV pays off.
maria: I'll add perf counters and a lightweight coordinator that selects KV layout at job start. fallback path: if mem margin < 8% then use TP-shard with async prefetch.
aj: can you also add a flag to force replicate-for-pp-stage for debug? e.g., `--force-pp-kv-repl`.
maria: yep, will add. patch plan:
- add `kv_layout_coordinator` (config + runtime decision)
- add perf counters and tracepoints (perf-bot should ingest)
- implement `nccl_grouping` and kernel selector
- add canary job in Dedicated cluster
runtime-ci: scheduled canary: job/kv-shard-canary-1783456890 on dedicated-prod starts in 10m :gear:
maria: quick checklist for the canary run:
- enable `nccl_grouping=true`
- toggle `kv_layout_coordinator` to replicate for PP stages
- enable `kernel_selector=auto`
olga: also run ablations: kernel-v5 vs v6, microbatch 4 vs 8, with/without prefetch.
sachin: I'll own the ablation matrix. will add JIRA ticket (RINF-1423) with params.
maria: one more datapoint: when sequence length tail is heavy (many short + few long), grouping small requests into a single prefix-cached path reduces KV pulls by ~30% — big win for latency-sensitive workloads.
aj: nice. any showstopper regressions?
maria: no hard stop. main risk: memory on smaller nodes. we'll gate by mem margin and default to TP-sharded in autoscale small configs.
olga: thanks. sync tomorrow 11am to review canary results.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
